html:
Nam tiến, the march to the south, is the name for the slow southward expansion of the Vietnamese from the Red River delta down the coast to the Mekong delta, from the 11th to the 18th century.

The Vietnamese took land from Champa step by step, in wars and by marriage deals, with the great blow coming at Vijaya in 1471. Soldiers and farmers settled each new strip. From the 1600s the Nguyễn lords of the south pushed on into the Khmer lands of the Mekong delta, where they founded Saigon in 1698.

By the mid 18th century Vietnam held the whole delta, at the cost of the Khmer and Cham peoples, many of whom still live there. The long new south, with its own dialect and trading towns such as Hội An, later fought the north in the civil wars that ended with Gia Long.
sum: Nam tiến, the march to the south, is the name for the slow southward expansion of the Vietnamese from the Red River delta down the coast to the Mekong delta, from the 11th to the 18th century.
